clue.text: See 17
Indianan mostly more difficult to please

explanation.surface: Someone from Indiana is pickier than most.
explanation.walkthrough: CHOOSIER loses its C. 'Mostly' usually cuts the last letter; here it is the first that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoosier is the long-established nickname for a native or resident of the US state of Indiana.

clue.text: Get stuck quite often by the main gates

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to become fixed or wedged somewhere, as a bone in the throat

definitions.text: quite often by the main gates
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the gatekeeper's house at the entrance to an estate, often found beside the gates

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a description rather than a synonym, which the blogger called a bit loose; 'quite often' hedges because not every one stands there.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means become firmly fixed; as a noun it is a small gatehouse at the entrance to a country estate.

clue.text: Structural feature of churches I start to contemplate

parts.note: the pipe organ is a fixture of most churches
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of contemplate

explanation.surface: Pondering an architectural detail of church buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Structural feature' reads as one phrase about architecture; the definition is the single word 'Structural'.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic can mean inherent in the fundamental constitution of a thing, so relating to its basic structure.

clue.text: Liverpool losing poor first half dismally

the first two of the four letters of poor

explanation.surface: A football report: Liverpool lost after a dismal, poor first half.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking PO out of LIVERPOOL leaves LIVEROL, which rearranges to ORVILLE. Orville was the green duckling puppet of ventriloquist Keith Harris.
explanation.definitionFit: Orville, a nappy-wearing green duckling who could not fly, was the puppet of British ventriloquist Keith Harris.

clue.text: Elite runners shamefully emigrate after missing opening parts of athletics tournament

indicators.note: acting shamefully means behaving out of line, so the letters are put out of order
missing says some letters are left out of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opening part of each word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of athletics
the first letter of tournament

explanation.surface: Star athletes disgracefully defect, skipping the start of a championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests sprinters, but here it means those who run a country. A and T come out of EMIGRATE before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is the ruling government of a country, the small elite group of people who run it.

clue.text: 21 down cannot possibly be heard

indicators.note: what can be heard is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: if something cannot possibly be so, it is so in no sense

explanation.surface: A claim that a puzzle answer is beyond hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: the answer to 21 down, naivety.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety and innocence are synonyms, both meaning a lack of worldly experience or guile.

clue.text: Rest of old wine gets drunk

indicators.note: someone drunk is unsteady and muddled, so the letters stagger out of order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The dregs of a vintage bottle get finished off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest of' looks like 'what remains of', but 'Rest' is a verb-phrase definition and 'of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a short rest is to recline on a bed or sofa for a while, often a nap.

clue.text: Stripped smart car at yard being joined together — just messing about!

indicators.note: stripped means with the outer layer removed, so the end letters go and the middle is kept

parts.note: a Cadillac is a smart car; its first two and last two letters are removed
yd is the abbreviation for yard
allying is joining together in alliance

explanation.surface: A car is broken for parts in a scrapyard, while someone fools about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart car' suggests the tiny Smart brand; it is a luxury Cadillac, with two letters stripped from each end.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilly-dally is to waste time through indecision or idling, so doing it is fooling about.

clue.text: Received praise for Rachel's new look

indicators.note: received here means taken in by the ear, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: the fodder, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Rachel's makeover earned her compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble supplies the definition: Lord Charles was the monocled dummy of ventriloquist Ray Alan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Charles, an upper-class drunken toff with a monocle, was the famous puppet of British ventriloquist Ray Alan.

clue.text: Almost ready for the table, joining the fish?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: losing consciousness under anaesthetic, nearly ready for the operating table
second meaning: sinking beneath the waves, down where the fish swim

explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' and 'fish' set up a dinner; the table is in an operating theatre and the fish are in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a patient slipping into anaesthesia before surgery and also a ship or person sinking below water.

clue.text: Mug made of crude copper taking a very long time

parts.note: pig is a crude, insulting slang word for a police officer
an eon is an immeasurably long period

explanation.surface: A cup made from unrefined metal takes ages to produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude copper' suggests unrefined metal (pig is also a casting of crude metal), but copper is a police officer, and crude marks rude slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for a gullible person easily cheated, a dupe who is readily taken in by a swindle.

clue.text: Hit with blow from the side of the hand involves the start of bleeding

parts.note: the opening letter of bleeding

explanation.walkthrough: The preamble supplies the definition: Lamb Chop was the sock-puppet lamb of American ventriloquist Shari Lewis.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb Chop, a sock puppet sheep, was the famous partner of American ventriloquist and children's entertainer Shari Lewis.

clue.text: What to wear to finish convention

parts.note: to dress stone or timber is to give it a smooth final finish
a code is a set of accepted conventions

explanation.surface: Deciding on an outfit for the closing day of a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convention' suggests a conference; it means an accepted rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress code is a set of rules telling people which clothes are acceptable for an event or workplace.

clue.text: Steward seen to clash with new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: At home French donkey is asinine

parts.note: someone at home is in
âne is French for donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey at home in France behaves like a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on asinine, which literally means donkey-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine and inane both mean extremely silly or foolish, lacking sense or meaning.

clue.text: Nylon line gets tangled around some itinerant herons

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters wrap themselves about the other piece
a tangled line is knotted out of its neat order, so those letters get jumbled

some of these words: the last letter of itinerant and the first two of herons, read across the gap

clue.text: Our name fails to gain entrance

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to fill them with delight, and to enamour is to make them fall in love.

clue.text: Angel lies about having godlike attributes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angel tells untruths regarding divine powers.
explanation.definitionFit: Omniscience, seeing and knowing everything, is a power traditionally ascribed to God, so the word describes a deity-like quality.

clue.text: Firm to stop the flow

definitions.meaning: first meaning: loyal and committed, unwavering

clue.text: Suspect more by stage one

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: It can come after Michaelmas time of year

clue.text: Bush's former presidential familiar has back trouble
